items.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I took Grover Washington seriously and he was grateful for that

ctx.x: Well a good listener and reader I think could profit from finding a critic or journalist that seems to be on the same wavelength as them, and if they like particular records it’s going to be a good chance that I’m going to enjoy that.

I think the consumer guide aspect of jazz journalism is valuable if it functions in that way. I like to be a little bit ahead of my readers. I hope I can suggest things to them that they haven’t though of before. I mean I want to be — not always provocative or inspiring but I want to be more insightful. I have a lot of experience listening. That’s what I try to do seriously for a living so I hope I can bring something to them they haven’t thought of before. of our vast experience. The networking aspect, the Jazz Journalists Association started in ’85 at a meeting in Chicago that brought together writers and broadcasters. I think it was sponsored by the NEA. And we decided that we should have some sort of organization, mostly just for networking purposes. So if we go to a city that we’re not familiar with for a festival we’ve got somebody to go out to dinner with. And it’s worked very well that way.
